title: Diputació de València pilots Metalesa's PlugSmart Pro system, which detects wild boar with cameras and lights warning signs on the CV-600 at Simat de la Valldigna
summary: Metalesa's PlugSmart Pro system uses cameras and detection algorithms to spot wild boar near the CV-600 road and light warning signs only when animals are present.
account: Europa Press reported on 12 February 2026, from a statement by the Diputació de València, on a set of pilot tests. The provincial council had begun them on the CV-600 road, in the area of Simat de la Valldigna and Benifairó de la Valldigna. The intelligent signaling system is designed to detect wild boar near the carriageway and automatically activate luminous warning signs. The Valencian road-safety company Metalesa carried out the work, with civil works by Grupo Bertolín. The system combines cameras with computer vision and automatic detection algorithms that identify animals passing. It activates dynamic luminous signs only when a real risk exists, and it is powered by photovoltaic energy. The council said that the system records crossing patterns, times and how often the signs light up. Council president Vicent Mompó visited the site with roads deputy Reme Mazzolari. He said that after some weeks the council would evaluate the results. If the system proved effective, the council would extend the model to the most sensitive stretches of the provincial network. No detection counts or accident figures are given. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the pilot as an aggregate benefit. Metalesa lists the Simat installation as a 2026 project for its PlugSmart Pro device. No evaluation or extension had been reported by late October 2026.
